stories.stat_label: kiwi moved back to the hills
stories.headline: Kiwi live wild around Wellington for the 1st time in 150 years
stories.summary: The Capital Kiwi Project, led with iwi and local landowners, moved 250+ kiwi back after trapping stoats. With chicks, there are now an estimated 300+ birds.
stories.why: Whole communities now help care for a bird many had never seen.

stories.stat_label: glass elevator up a cliff face
stories.headline: A 288 m cliff elevator cuts kids' school trip to 30 minutes
stories.summary: Children aged 6 to 15 used to spend about 6 hours a day walking to a mountaintop school and back. A glass elevator up the canyon wall now gets them there in about half an hour.
stories.why: Kids get hours of their day back, and a much safer route.

stories.headline: A 6-year-old's $768 lemonade stand grew into $5M+ of help
stories.summary: Payton Obert set up a stand in 2018 to buy toys for kids in hospital, after a teddy bear comforted her there. Her nonprofit has since raised over $5 million in cash and goods.
stories.why: It now supports more than 40 local groups helping children.

stories.stat_label: lakes made from old coal pits
stories.headline: Germany turned 23 old coal mines into a lake district
stories.summary: Flooded lignite pits in Lusatia now form 23 lakes with about 14,000 hectares of water. In 2026, five of them were linked into one connected waterway for boats.
stories.why: A scarred coal region is becoming a place for swimming, boating and wildlife.

fun_fact: Kiwi chicks can usually fend off stoats once they reach about 1 kg.
